summary: Specifies Update Notification messages that let the local mobility anchor in a Proxy Mobile IPv6 domain asynchronously tell the mobile access gateway about changes to a mobility session, using a new Mobility Header message type. This helps keep the two ends of the mobility system in sync.

plainLanguage.summary: The main office can send a quick note to the local office when something changes.

questions: what is a proxy mobile ipv6 update notification
what is the mobility header type 19
subtitle: A way for the local mobility anchor in Proxy Mobile IPv6 to push change notices to a mobile access gateway.

tldr.problem: In Proxy Mobile IPv6, once a mobility session is set up the local mobility anchor (LMA) has no general way to tell the mobile access gateway (MAG) that the session or its policies have changed.
tldr.mechanism: Two new Mobility Header messages, Update Notification (type 19) and Update Notification Acknowledgement (type 20), let the LMA send a reason code and mobility options, and optionally get a status back.
tldr.outcome: The LMA can ask a MAG to re-register a session, apply new session parameters, handle a vendor-specific request or report access network parameters, without short session lifetimes and their extra signaling.

today: RFC 7077 is a Proposed Standard from November 2013 and has not been obsoleted or updated. It extends the Proxy Mobile IPv6 base specification, RFC 5213.

sections.title: Why Notifications Are Needed
sections.content:
Proxy Mobile IPv6 (RFC 5213) is a network-based mobility protocol. It gives a mobile node IP mobility support without the node taking part in any mobility signaling. Two entities do the work: the local mobility anchor (LMA) and the mobile access gateway (MAG). The MAG starts a session with a Proxy Binding Update and the LMA answers with a Proxy Binding Acknowledgement.

After that, the base protocol has no way for the LMA to tell the MAG about changes. The existing Heartbeat message (RFC 5847) and Binding Revocation message (RFC 5846) are each built for one specific purpose and are not enough for a notification framework.

One use is asking the MAG to re-register a session. Short session lifetimes could do something similar, but in several networks that means an unacceptable and mostly unnecessary rise in signaling load. Another use is a change in a QoS policy, an IP flow mobility policy or an IPv4 traffic offload policy (RFC 6909), where the LMA wants the MAG to re-register so the policies are updated.
sections.plainLanguage: Right now the main office can only wait for the local office to call. This lets the main office send a note first when something changes, instead of making the local office call all the time.

sections.title: Two Usage Examples
sections.content:
In the first example the LMA wants a MAG to re-register a session. After the mobile node attaches and the Proxy Binding Update and Acknowledgement are exchanged and the tunnel is set up, the LMA sends an Update Notification with reason FORCE-REREGISTRATION. The MAG acknowledges it and then sends a new Proxy Binding Update, which the LMA answers.

In the second, the LMA wants to give the MAG updated session parameters, for example a new QoS profile or IPv4 offload policy. It sends an Update Notification with reason UPDATE-SESSION-PARAMETERS, the MAG acknowledges, and the MAG applies the new policy option.
sections.plainLanguage: Either the main office says 'please fill in your forms again', or it says 'here are the new rules' and the local office starts following them.

sections.title: The Two Message Formats
sections.content:
The Update Notification (UPN) has Mobility Header type 19. Its fields are a 16-bit Sequence Number, a 16-bit Notification Reason, an Acknowledgement Requested (A) flag, a Retransmit (D) flag, a reserved field that is set to 0 and ignored on receipt, and then mobility options.

The Sequence Number lets the LMA match an acknowledgement to its notification, and implementations MUST avoid collisions among all outstanding notifications. The (D) flag is cleared the first time a Sequence Number is sent and set on retransmissions, so the receiver can spot duplicates. The options field is padded so the whole Mobility Header is a multiple of 8 octets, and a receiver MUST ignore and skip options it does not understand.

The Update Notification Acknowledgement (UPA) has type 20. It carries the copied 16-bit Sequence Number, an 8-bit Status Code, a reserved field and mobility options. Status codes 0 to 127 mean the notification was processed successfully, and 128 to 255 mean an error occurred.
sections.plainLanguage: The note has a number so replies can be matched to it, a reason, and a tick box asking 'please write back'. The reply repeats the number and says whether it worked.

sections.title: Reason and Status Codes
sections.content:
The Notification Reason is an enumeration with no internal structure. Defined values are 1 FORCE-REREGISTRATION (send a Proxy Binding Update for the session), 2 UPDATE-SESSION-PARAMETERS (apply the parameters carried in the message), 3 VENDOR-SPECIFIC-REASON (handling follows the Vendor-Specific Mobility options of RFC 5094) and 4 ANI-PARAMS-REQUESTED (send the currently known Access Network Identifier parameters, see RFC 6757). Values 0 and 255 are reserved.

The defined status codes are 0 SUCCESS, 128 FAILED-TO-UPDATE-SESSION-PARAMETERS and 129 MISSING-VENDOR-SPECIFIC-OPTION.
sections.plainLanguage: The reason is a short code for why the note was sent, like 'redo your forms' or 'new rules'. The answer code says 'done' or 'could not do it'.

sections.title: LMA and MAG Behavior
sections.content:
The LMA MUST include either the Mobile Node Identifier option (RFC 4283) for one session or the Mobile Node Group Identifier option (RFC 6602) for a set of sessions. If no Group Identifier was negotiated, the value 1 can always be used and identifies all sessions between that LMA and MAG. The LMA MAY add a modified parameter as a mobility option, such as an IPv4 traffic offload or QoS option. The Sequence Number starts at a random value and increases monotonically, wrapping to 0 at the maximum. For FORCE-REREGISTRATION or ANI-PARAMS-REQUESTED it is RECOMMENDED that the (A) flag be 0.

If an acknowledgement is requested and none arrives, the LMA MUST retransmit with the same Sequence Number and contents and the (D) flag set. It waits at least MIN_DELAY_BETWEEN_UPDATE_NOTIFICATION_REPLAY (default 1000 milliseconds) between retransmits, and retransmits up to MAX_UPDATE_NOTIFICATION_RETRANSMIT_COUNT times (default 1). After that the message MUST be discarded and the event SHOULD be logged. A Binding Error with Status 2 means the MAG does not support the message, and the LMA MUST NOT send more notifications to it unless an administrative action is taken. An acknowledgement whose Sequence Number matches nothing MUST be discarded.

The MAG MUST verify the Mobility Header as in Section 9.2 of RFC 6275 and check that the message is protected by the security association used for its other signaling. A retransmission, seen by Sequence Number and (D) flag, MUST NOT be treated as a new request, but if the (A) flag is set the MAG MUST always respond. Then it acts on the reason:

  • FORCE-REREGISTRATION: send a Proxy Binding Update to get the updated parameters.
  • UPDATE-SESSION-PARAMETERS: apply the options. If it cannot, it drops and logs the message when (A) is 0, or answers with status 128 when (A) is 1.
  • VENDOR-SPECIFIC-REASON: handle the Vendor-Specific Mobility option. If none is present, it drops and logs when (A) is 0, or answers with status 129 when (A) is 1.
  • ANI-PARAMS-REQUESTED: send a Proxy Binding Update with the Access Network Identifier option reflecting current access network parameters.

Other reasons are left to the documents that define them. When acknowledging, the MAG copies the Sequence Number and the identifier option, sets the Status, and swaps the source and destination addresses of the notification.
sections.plainLanguage: The main office keeps asking a limited number of times and then gives up. The local office checks the note is real, does what it says, and writes back if asked.

sections.title: Transport and Security
sections.content:
Over IPv4, the Mobility Header is carried in UDP with destination port 5436. Over IPv6, the Mobility Header is part of the IPv6 headers. If IPsec ESP is used, it is applied in transport mode.

Both messages MUST be protected by the same mechanism as the other Proxy Mobile IPv6 signaling between that LMA and MAG. With IPsec, the same security association that protects the Proxy Binding Update and Acknowledgement must protect these messages, and after rekeying the new association is used. The traffic selectors in the Security Policy Database entry have to be extended to include Mobility Header types 19 and 20.
sections.plainLanguage: The notes travel in the same locked envelope as all the other messages between those two offices.

sections.title: IANA Registries
sections.content:
IANA allocated Mobility Header types 19 (Update Notification) and 20 (Update Notification Acknowledgement). It also created two registries under "Mobile IPv6 Parameters": the Update Notification Reasons Registry and the Update Notification Acknowledgement Status Registry. Both use the "Specification Required" allocation policy.

The configuration variables for retransmission count and delay must be configurable by system management, and their values have to survive reboots and service restarts. The suggested range for the retransmit count is 0 to 5 and for the delay is 500 to 5000 milliseconds.
sections.plainLanguage: Two new lists were started so everyone agrees what each reason number and answer number means.

items.label: FORCE-REREGISTRATION
items.desc: MAG re-registers the session with a Proxy Binding Update.

items.label: UPDATE-SESSION-PARAMETERS
items.desc: MAG applies the parameters carried in the message.

items.label: VENDOR-SPECIFIC-REASON
items.desc: Handled per the Vendor-Specific Mobility options.

items.label: ANI-PARAMS-REQUESTED
items.desc: MAG reports Access Network Identifier parameters.

items.label: FAILED-TO-UPDATE-SESSION-PARAMETERS (status)
items.desc: The MAG could not apply the session parameters.

items.label: MISSING-VENDOR-SPECIFIC-OPTION (status)
items.desc: A required Vendor-Specific Mobility option was absent.
